text: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words."

versions.text: "Go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two verbs, קוּם ("arise/get up") followed by וְיָרַדְתָּ ("and go down"). The opening imperative is dropped in the current rendering; restoring it preserves the urgency and the rhythm of the command.

text: So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
But the vessel he was shaping from the clay was ruined in his hands, so he made it over into another vessel, whatever seemed right to him.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares the LORD. Look, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
If at any moment I speak against a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, tear it down, and destroy it,
and that nation I have warned turns from its evil, then I will relent of the disaster I intended to bring on it.

versions.text: and that nation turns from its evil, then I will relent of the disaster I intended to bring on it.
versions.explanation: The clause אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתִּי עָלָיו ("against which I have spoken") is missing. It ties the nation's repentance to the prior announcement of judgment in verse 7 and should be represented.

text: And if at any moment I speak about a nation or a kingdom, to build it up and plant it,
but it does what is evil in my eyes and will not listen to my voice, then I will relent of the good I had promised to do for it.

Now say to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.
But they say, "It is hopeless. We will follow our own plans; each of us will act on the stubbornness of his evil heart."
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Ask among the nations—who has ever heard the like? Virgin Israel has done a thing too horrible for words.
Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave the rocky slopes? Do the cold waters that flow from the mountains ever run dry?

versions.text: Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave the rocky slopes? Do the cold, flowing streams ever run dry?
versions.explanation: The adjective זָרִים ("foreign, from elsewhere/from afar") is left untranslated. Including the sense of waters coming from distant heights completes the image of unfailing mountain streams.

text: Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to worthless idols. They have been made to stumble in their ways, off the ancient roads, to walk on side paths, on a road never paved,

versions.text: Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to worthless idols. They have stumbled off their paths, off the ancient roads, to walk on trails, on a way not built up,
versions.explanation: וַיַּכְשִׁלוּם is a causative (hiphil) form — the idols cause the people to stumble; the current rendering makes it simply intransitive and loses the agency of the false worship. Also "a way not built up" is awkward English for לֹא סְלוּלָה ("not paved, no highway").

text: making their land a desolation, an object of endless scorn. All who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.
Like a wind from the east I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, on the day of their calamity.

Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will never be lost from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor a word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him down with the tongue and pay no attention to anything he says."
Give heed to me, LORD; listen to what my accusers are saying!
Should evil be the payment for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you and spoke on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.

So hand their children over to famine; deliver them to the power of the sword. Let their wives be left childless and widowed; let their men be struck down by death, their young men cut down by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them—for they have dug a pit to catch me and hidden snares for my feet.
But you, LORD, know all their plots to kill me. Do not cover over their guilt or blot out their sin from your sight. Let them be overthrown before you; deal with them in the time of your anger.
